title: Punish Early Queen Attacks
subtitle: Defend against Scholar's Mate and gain time doing it.

steps.say: Every beginner meets this: 2.Qh5!?, hunting the four-move checkmate on f7. Don't panic — early queen sorties are BAD chess, and today you'll learn to prove it: defend calmly, develop with every move, and watch the queen become a target.

steps.prompt: The queen eyes both e5 and f7. Defend the REAL threat — and develop while you do it.
hints: f7 is still guarded by your king — the immediate threat is Qxe5+, snacking your center pawn with check.
One knight move defends e5 and develops toward the center.

line.say: Calm and strong — e5 is defended, a piece is developed, and White's queen has achieved nothing. Defense with development is the whole recipe.

rejections.say: Qxe5+! Check — and the queen forks your h8 rook through the hole you just opened. The e5 pawn was the real threat, not f7.
Qxe5+ wins the pawn with check. The knight attacked the queen but forgot the job: e5 needed a defender first.

steps.wrongSay: Ask what the queen actually threatens THIS move — then defend it while developing.
steps.successSay: Rule one against early queens: no panic, just development that defends.

steps.prompt: Now the bishop joins the queen against f7 — checkmate is threatened! Find the ONE move that stops everything.
hints: Queen and bishop both aim at f7: Qxf7 would be MATE. You must break the queen's path to f7.
One pawn move blocks the h5–f7 diagonal AND attacks the queen. Two jobs, one move.

line.say: Exactly! The pawn slams the diagonal shut AND kicks the queen — she must retreat and White has already lost time. Defense has never felt so aggressive.

rejections.say: Qxf7# — the four-move checkmate! The knight blocked nothing on the h5–f7 diagonal. Against a mate threat, only moves that stop the mate count.
Qxf7# — checkmate! Yes, your knight attacked the queen, but mate outranks every threat in chess. Parry first.
Qxf7# — still mate! The queen covers d7 and e7 along the seventh rank, so opening d7 saved nothing. Block the diagonal with g6.

steps.wrongSay: Checkmate on f7 is threatened — only a move that blocks the h5–f7 diagonal (with tempo!) saves the day.
steps.successSay: One modest pawn move refuted the most famous trap in chess. Remember g6 forever.

steps.prompt: The queen re-aims at f7 down the f-file. Shut the attack down for good — with development!
hints: Qf3 + Bc4 hit f7 again. This time the attack line is the f-FILE — put a piece in the way.
Your g8 knight's natural developing square happens to block the file perfectly.

line.say: The f-file is blocked, the knight is developed, and White's 'attack' is officially over — three queen moves for nothing while you built an army. This is why early queen raids fail.

rejections.say: Qxf7# — checkmate again! The knight attacked the queen from a proud square, but the f-file stayed open. The mate threat ALWAYS comes first.
exd5 — White captures, the bishop's diagonal reopens with the threat renewed, and you're a pawn down. Block the f-file with the knight instead.

steps.wrongSay: The mate threat runs down the f-file now. Which developing move physically blocks it?
steps.successSay: Three threats parried, three pieces developed. Count the tempo: you're winning the opening race 3–0.

steps.prompt: The stubborn queen swings to b3, plotting Bxf7+ once more. Time to punish her — attack the queen with a threat she can't ignore!
hints: Chasing the queen is only great when your chasing move ALSO does something. Look for a knight jump with a nasty follow-up.
From d4 the knight hits the queen AND eyes c2 — the fork square of king and rook.

line.say: Brutal! The queen is attacked and Nxc2+ — royal-forking king and rook — hangs over White's head. The 'attacker' now scrambles to survive. That's the full punishment for early queen raids.

rejections.say: It hits the queen, but from the rim with no follow-up — she steps aside and shrugs. Nd4 attacks her AND threatens the c2 fork: chase with purpose.
Bxf7+! The bishop is untouchable — the queen guards it straight through the now-empty diagonal — and your king is dragged into the open. The pawn grab walked into White's one real threat.

steps.wrongSay: Attack the queen — with the knight move that carries a threat of its own.
steps.successSay: Defended, developed, and now attacking: the complete anti-queen-raid masterclass. White's opening is in ruins.
